RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the August 4, 2005/Sravana 13, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal;
Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs; Personnel, Public
Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Science and Technology; Shipping, Road
Transport and Highways; Small Scale Industries; Space; Statistics and
Programme Implementation; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions —20
Sale of former Indian Embassy
Building in Bonne
*161. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of  EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to sell 100 years old former Indian Embassy
Building in Bonne, Germany despite strong
objection from the Indian community in
Germany;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the advertisement for selling
this building appeared in the Daily
Newspaper and the website in Germany; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Miners killed in coal mine accidents
†*162. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of miners killed in
accidents during the last one year in coal
mines operating under subsidiary coal
companies of Coal India Limited in
Jharkhand;
(b) the findings of the Enquiry
Committees constituted for conducting
enquiry into such accidents from time to time;
(c) the number of officials found
responsible for such accidents against
whom action has been taken; and
(d) the steps taken to check such
accidents?
Government representatives in ILO
Conference
†*163. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of  LABOUR
AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government sends
representatives of labourers in the I.L.O.
(International Labour Organisation)
Conference;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

50
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the criteria adopted to grant
permission to representatives for
participating in the Conference;
(c) whether Government had sent
representatives of labourers in the 93rd
International Labour Conference, recently
held in Geneva;
(d) if so, the aim with which these
representatives had been sent in the above
Conference;
(e) whether it is a fact that Government
had received a proposal from the
International Labour Organisation for
sending the representatives of labourers in
this Conference; and
(f) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government in this regard?
Access to Indians in Pakistani jails
*164. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of  EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Indians held in
Pakistan presently on various charges;
(b) whether Government have any
access to these Indians;
(c) what steps Government propose to
take to ensure that there is regular
communication among these Indian
prisoners and their families in India;
(d) whether any agreement has been
worked out with Pakistan to humanize this
issue; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Safeguarding interests of Indian IT
companies
*165. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
unscrupulous operators are perpetrating
frauds and duping unsuspecting Indian
companies by giving BPO (Branching
Process Operations) work from Indian or
overseas clients;
(b) if so, whether our existing laws are
adequate to deal with such a situation with
a view to safeguarding interests of Indian
IT companies;
(c) how many such cases were brought
to the notice of Government during 2004
and first six months of 2005;
(d) whether any guidelines have been
issued for the protection of interests of
Indian Companies; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Widening of highways in Tamil Nadu
*166. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
Minister of  SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had accorded its approval for converting
the Madurai-Aruppukottai-Tuticorin
Highway into a four lane road;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the other National Highways in
Tamil Nadu that are being converted into
four or six lane for which accord had been
given, recently?
Expansion of communication services
in Orissa
†*167. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
Will the Minister of  COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of

provide communication services at a fast
speed in the State and what is the outcome
thereof;
(c) by when Orissa is likely to be
brought under cent-per cent communication
services; and

Financial assistance to craftsmen and
weavers
†1109. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether the target has been fixed by
Government to give financial assistance to
craftsmen and weavers under the Self
Employment Credit Card Scheme; and
(b) if so, the number of craftsmen and
weavers who have been benefited, so far
under this scheme, year-wise and
State-wise?
ARIs under REGP in NER
1110. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have
established agro and rural industries in
North-Eastern Region with special
reference to Assam under the Rural
Employment Generation Programme during
the last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(c) the funds allocated for this purpose
and the steps taken for the implementation
of this programme?
Livelihood from ARIs
1111. SHRI N.R. GOVINDRAJAR:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of population earning
livelihood from Agriculture and Agro
Industries in the country, particularly in
Tamil Nadu;
(b) whether Government are making
additional efforts to promote agro based
industries; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

253
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Enriched uranium from non-NSG
countries
1112. SHRI NILOTPAL BASU: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are in pursuit
for enriched uranium and transfer of dual
use technologies for nuclear programme;
(b) whether this would require a
considerable period of time because of the
existing agreement among the Nuclear
Suppliers Group and the existing legislation
of some of the member countries;
(c) if so, whether country is looking for
enriched uranium from non-NSG countries;
and
(d) whether mandatory inspection by
IAEA suppliers of technologies of fissile
material insist on the basis of extant
agreements and legislations which would
adversely affect our fast breeder reactor
project which is a top priority in terms of
autonomy in development?
Rehabilitation of displaced persons
1113. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the number of memoranda regarding
rehabilitation submitted  by Project
Affected Families (PAF) of Pofran and
Akkarpatti villages, situated at coastal side
of Palaghar Tehsil of Thane district in
Maharashtra, after their evacuation by
Tarapur Nuclear Power Station authorities;
(b) whether Mumbai High Court in an
interim order dated 1st October, 2004 (Writ
Petition No. 5663 of 2004) had directed
specific reliefs and rehabilitation measures
for the PAF;
(c) if so, the status of implementation
of directives from the Court; and
(d) measures taken to address the issues
raised in the Petition?
US officials visit to the nuclear
installations in India
1114. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a visit of
Members of Atomic Power Regulatory
Authority of the US to the nuclear
installations in India was organized in
February, 2005;
(b) if so, the details and purpose of the
said visit;
(c) whether besides the US officials, of
which other countries were accorded the
privilege of visiting our nuclear installations
in the past alongwith the details of each
visit;
(d) whether such visits are organized
on reciprocal basis; and
(e) if so, the details of visits by the
officials of the Indian nuclear
establishments to the nuclear installations
in the US and in other countries?
Coal production from private sector
coal blocks
†1115. SHRI SURENDRA LATH:
SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
has to allot 168 coal blocks to private sector
out of which 75 blocks have been allotted
but only 11 of them have started
production;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that

254
these private entrepreneurs who had taken
the said blocks for establishing industry,
have not established the same, so far, and
the coal is being sold directly in markets as
a result of which it is causing losses to
Government worth hundreds of crores of
rupees; and
(c) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to avoid the said situation?
